name: Mechanized Infantry
role: High-mobility infantry operating alongside armoured formations in Infantry Combat Vehicles, combining the firepower and protection of armoured vehicles with the versatility of foot soldiers for rapid, deep battlefield deployment.
history: Concept originated post-1965 Indo-Pakistani War to give infantry high-speed mobility alongside armoured tank formations.
In 1949, the Brigade of the Guards was raised as the first elite all-India mixed arm regiment, later converting to mechanised role.
In 1979, General K. Sundarji spearheaded bringing 14 mechanised battalions under a single regimental identity: The Mechanised Infantry Regiment.
Participated with distinction in Operation Pawan (Sri Lanka), Operation Rakshak (Punjab), Operation Vijay (Kargil), and UN Peacekeeping missions.
